summary: DTE Electric, which serves about two million Michigan customers, comments in support of MISO's October 2 LARS filing and asks FERC to accept it as proposed, citing its entry requirements and its role in answering the show cause order.
ask: Accept MISO's LARS filing as proposed.

points.point: DTE Electric supports LARS as a reasonable way to evaluate load additions and paired generation.
points.quote: DTE Electric supports MISO's proposal and believes the LARS framework represents a reasonable approach to evaluating the transmission, operational, and resource adequacy impacts

points.point: Studying load and generation together can show different impacts than stand-alone studies.
points.quote: jointly planned and electrically proximate resources may produce materially different system impacts than traditional stand-alone studies.

points.point: DTE points to deposit, size, site control and pairing requirements as safeguards against speculative requests.
points.quote: Participating projects must satisfy applicable deposit, minimum size, site control, and commercial operation requirements.

points.point: DTE notes any eligible entity may be the interconnection customer for the generation.
points.quote: permitting the interconnection customer responsible for the generation component to be any eligible entity

throughLine.text: Supports MISO's LARS filing as compliance with the E-8 show cause order, which DTE says directs a just and reasonable framework for integrating large and co-located loads.
